note.title: Complete comprehension
note.overview: This note supports 7 source-backed questions on Complete comprehension.
learningGoals: Identify the grammatical clue and apply it accurately.
mustMemoriseRules: Translate the verb and every case-controlled noun.

workedExamples.why: servus laborat means “the slave works”. The nominative servus is the subject.
canis dormit means “the dog sleeps”. The nominative canis is the subject.
servus canem portat means “the slave carries the dog”. The accusative canem receives the action.

workedExamples.answer: the slave gives a letter to the brother
workedExamples.why: servus epistulam fratri dat means “the slave gives a letter to the brother”. The dative fratri means “to the brother”.
ad hortum ambulat means “he/she walks to the garden”. ad takes the accusative for movement towards.

commonMistakes: Recognising the meaning but submitting an incomplete form or spelling.

detailedExplanation: This note supports 7 source-backed questions on Complete comprehension.

Translate in grammatical stages: find the finite verb, identify the subject, locate objects and recipients from their cases, attach prepositional phrases, preserve tense, and only then write natural English.
examTips: Mark the finite verb first, then use noun endings to assign subject, object and recipient roles.
Normal Latin word order can vary; the case, number, gender, person and tense endings cannot.
For English to Latin, build each required form before arranging the sentence.
